questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Belize?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Belize on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Belize article.

questions.proof: It shares a border on the north with the Mexican state of Quintana Roo, on the west with the Guatemalan department of Petén, and on the south with the Guatemalan department of Izabal.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Belize on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Belize on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Belize?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belize article.

questions.proof: Belmopan, which is near the centre of the country, is its capital.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Belize about 22,966 square kilometres; Kiribati about 811 square kilometres; Tonga about 749 square kilometres; Federated States of Micronesia about 702 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Belmopan?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Belize is Belmopan.
